# Copilot instructions

## Repository layout and commands

- The runnable application is in `src/`, not the repository root. Run package commands from `src/`.
- Install dependencies with `npm ci` (the lockfile is `src/package-lock.json`).
- Start the local Next.js development server with `npm run dev`, then open `http://localhost:3000`.
- Create a production build with `npm run build`; serve an existing build with `npm run start`.
- Run the configured ESLint check with `npm run lint`.
- Run a focused lint check with `npx eslint app/page.tsx` (replace the path with the file being changed).
- Run the TypeScript check with `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- There is currently no test script, test directory, or test framework, so there is no single-test command. Do not add test commands to changes unless a test runner is introduced.

## Architecture

- This is a Next.js 16 App Router application using React Server Components by default. Route files live under `src/app/`; `src/app/page.tsx` is the home route and `src/app/not-found.tsx` is the custom 404 route.
- `src/app/layout.tsx` is the global shell: it loads Google fonts, global CSS, the theme provider, the navigation bar, and the decorative background before rendering route content. Keep site-wide UI here rather than duplicating it in individual pages.
- `ThemeProvider` and `ThemeToggle` are client components because they use `next-themes`, browser state, and the View Transitions API. Keep browser-only behavior behind a `"use client"` boundary and preserve the unmounted placeholder in `ThemeToggle` to avoid hydration differences.
- `Navbar` owns the site navigation and links to `/`, `/projects`, and `/blog`. New routes should align with those links and the App Router structure.
- `PaintStrokes` provides fixed, pointer-events-disabled SVG decoration for light and dark themes. It is presentational background UI and should not become part of page layout or interaction.
- Styling is Tailwind CSS v4 through `src/app/globals.css` and `@tailwindcss/postcss`; the CSS file also defines the shadcn theme variables and custom dark variant. `src/components.json` configures shadcn with the `@/components`, `@/lib`, and `@/components/ui` aliases.
- The `@/*` alias resolves from `src/`. Use it for imports such as `@/components/...` and `@/lib/...`; `src/lib/utils.ts` exports `cn`, which combines `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` for conditional class names.
- Static assets belong in `src/public/` and are referenced from the site root (for example, `/pixel-cat.jpg`). Use `next/image` for raster assets in rendered pages.

## Conventions specific to this repository

- Follow the existing App Router server/client split: pages, layout, navigation, and decorative components remain server components unless they need browser APIs or hooks; theme integration stays in the client components.
- Use the existing design tokens and utility classes from `globals.css` instead of introducing a second styling system or a separate Tailwind config. Preserve the light/dark behavior driven by the `.dark` class from `next-themes`.
- Use `next/link` for internal navigation and `next/image` for local images. Keep interactive controls accessible with an explicit `aria-label`, as done by the theme toggle.
- The project uses the `base-maia` shadcn style, CSS variables, Lucide as its configured icon library, and no Tailwind prefix. New shadcn components should follow `src/components.json` rather than adding ad hoc configuration.
- `src/AGENTS.md` is generated by Next.js and is intentionally committed. Keep its Next.js agent-rules block intact; `next dev` may re-add it if removed. Before making Next-specific changes, consult the relevant installed guidance under `src/node_modules/next/dist/docs/`.
